root.name: Three Knights Opening: Steinitz-Rosenthal Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 g6 4. d4 exd4 5. Nd5

overview: After 3...g6 4.d4 exd4 White plays 5.Nd5, putting the knight on the outpost and threatening Nxc7+. Black can play ...Bg7 and ...d6 or ...Nxe4, and White regains d4. The play is open and tactical but not heavily theoretical.

white_ideas.idea: Use the Nd5 outpost and regain d4 with Nxd4

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after d4 exchanges, Black kingside fianchetto

character.notes: Open play with tactics around d5 and c7 but not extreme.

gambit.notes: Black's pawn on d4 is regained by Nxd4.

character.reason: Open tactical game that is neither especially solid nor forced.

gambit.reason: White regains d4 so no pawn is given.

structure.reason: The e- and d-pawns come off and lines open for the pieces.

level.reason: Some tactics and plans to learn.

plans.reason: White's knight settles on d5 and Black develops a kingside fianchetto.
